newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's Lion Brewery announces IPO.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's Lion Brewery announces IPO.

text.p: The Lion Brewery Ceylon Ltd will make an initial public offer (IPO) of 12.5 million shares at 20 rupees, which will open on the stock exchange on November 28, a the company said in a statement.
The new company, a subsidiary of Ceylon Brewery Ltd, wants to raise 500 million rupees to build a new brewery with an initial installed capacity of 30 million litres per year, the firm said.
"The 500 million rupees will come from the IPO, Ceylon Brewery's stake of 50.4 percent, and from Carlsberg which is taking 24.6 percent," said Suresh Shah, chief executive of both local companies.
Carlsberg has an eight percent stake in Ceylon Brewery, which also brews Guinness under licence.
Existing shareholders of Ceylon Brewery will be given preference when allotting shares in the IPO, on the basis of seven new shares for every 10 held, the firm said.
"But the issue will close once it is fully subscribed, whether Ceylon Brewery sharehodlers have subscribed or not," Shah told Reuters.
The new plant, to be located 24 km from Colombo, was needed because sales had soared after the government cut the excise tax on beer by 70 percent in late 1995, Shah said.
